body.answer: Intel Extreme Masters China 2026 is scheduled to run from November 2 to November 8, 2026 and will be held as a LAN event in China. The week-long timing makes it a compact, high-intensity stop on the IEM circuit, which often attracts top international teams and regional contenders. Hosting the event in China is significant for local fan engagement and can influence broadcast windows and on-site atmosphere compared with European or North American stops.

body.answer: Official materials list a total prize pool of $1,000,000, however the currently published prize breakdown accounts for $300,000 with first place listed at $125,000 and the top three combined at $205,000; tournament organizers have not yet clarified the discrepancy. Regardless, the listed payouts show meaningful rewards across the field, with money extending down to 16th place in the published breakdown, which helps teams cover operating costs and rewards deeper runs. The exact distribution and any adjustments will matter for team budgets and player earnings, so keep an eye on official announcements.

body.answer: Yes — the event is confirmed as a LAN event in China, which matters a lot for competitive integrity and spectacle. LAN conditions remove online variance like ping and connectivity issues, allowing teams’ raw tactical executions and mechanical skill to shine, and they typically produce the most memorable matches and highlight plays. For players and organizations, LAN performance often carries heavier weight in scouting and market value than online results.
